rationale: Engineering teams at AI-forward companies are the buyer — they have budget and pay for CI/CD tooling (GitHub Actions, CircleCI), confirming willingness to pay. However, building an actual agent-aware CI/CD layer is deep infrastructure work requiring custom integrations with multiple LLM coding agents, CI systems, and runtime environments — this is a 6-18 month product build, not a Claude prompt plus a landing page. Operational autonomy is also very low because each customer's stack is different and meaningful setup/support per customer is unavoidable. The idea should be dropped until a much narrower slice (e.g. a specific agent + a specific CI system) is identified.
solution_plan: This is not viable for a solo non-technical operator with this factory. The core need — a new CI/CD orchestration layer that understands agent-driven code — requires deep engineering, SDK integrations with multiple coding agents (Cursor, Devin, etc.), and bespoke CI pipeline plugins. There is no way to deliver this as a Claude prompt plus a web form. A solo operator could not build, sell, or maintain it without a full engineering team. If Youval wanted to stay adjacent, the only realistic option would be a very narrow consulting/diagnostic report ("audit your current CI for agent readiness"), but that would require human-delivered work per client, making it low-autonomy and low-scale. Not recommended.
